| Greek | `l` | `i` | avoided on purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| πολυδάκρυτος (πολυδάκρυτος δέ τοι ἔσται, 24.620) | "much-wept" | "much wept for" | "of many tears" (kept for πολυδάκρυος, 17.192, which is active-sounding), "tearful", "to be mourned at length"; δακρυτός is passive, so the son is the one wept for |
| κτερεϊζέμεν (24.657) | "give funeral rites to" | "hold funeral rites for" | "bury" (kept for θάπτω), "honour with gifts", "perform the obsequies"; κτερεΐζω is from κτέρεα, the funeral offerings |
| ἀστυβοώτης (κῆρυξ ἀστυβοώτης, 24.701) | "the town-shouter" | "the town-crier" | "town-caller", "city-shouter"; ἄστυ + βοάω "shout" |
| ἄντα ἐῴκει (24.630) | "seen straight on, … like" | "seen straight on, he was like" | "face to face" (reserved for ἀντίον), "to the face", "in appearance"; ἄντα "straight on" |
| ἐν φόνῳ (κέατ’ ἐν φόνῳ, 24.610) | "in slaughter" | "in their blood" | "in gore", "in death"; φόνος "killing, bloodshed" (cf. ἀνδροφόνος "man-slaying") |
| ὠκὺς Ἀχιλλεύς (24.621, without πόδας) | "swift Achilles" | "swift Achilles" | "fleet", "quick"; πόδας ὠκύς stays "swift in feet" / "swift of foot" |
| τὸν δ’ ἐπικερτομέων προσέφη πόδας ὠκὺς Ἀχιλλεύς (24.649, whole-line speech introduction) | "And him, taunting, addressed swift-in-feet Achilles:" | "Taunting him, Achilles, swift of foot, said to him:" | "answered" (reserved for ἠμείβετο), "mocking"; follows the Odyssey row τὸν δ’ ἐπικερτομέων προσέφης (22.194) |
| τὸν δ’ αὖτε προσέειπε ποδάρκης δῖος Ἀχιλλεύς (24.668, whole-line reply-formula) | "And him in turn addressed swift-footed, heavenly Achilles:" | "Then swift-footed, heavenly Achilles spoke to him in turn:" | "answered" (reserved for ἠμείβετο); follows the table's τὸν δ’ αὖτε προσέειπε rows and ποδάρκης δῖος Ἀχιλλεύς (1.121) |
| τὸν πρότερος προσέειπε γέρων Πρίαμος θεοειδής (24.634, whole-line speech introduction) | "Him first addressed the old man Priam, godlike in form:" | "Priam, the old man, godlike in form, spoke to him first:" | "answered"; follows the table's τὸν πρότερος προσέειπεν Ἀλέξανδρος θεοειδής (6.517), with the published Priam rendering of γέρων Πρίαμος θεοειδής (without the hyphen in `l`) |
| Ἠὼς δὲ κροκόπεπλος ἐκίδνατο πᾶσαν ἐπ’ αἶαν (24.695, the δέ form of the dawn-formula) | "and Dawn, saffron-robed, was spreading herself over all the earth," | "and Dawn in her saffron robe was spreading over all the earth," | follows the table's Ἠὼς μὲν κροκόπεπλος … (8.1), with δέ "and" for μέν "for her part" |
| λέξον με (λέξον νῦν με τάχιστα διοτρεφές, 24.635, "put me to bed") | "Lay me down" | "Put me to bed" | "let me lie down" (middle), "make me sleep"; λέγω in its old sense "lay down"; the Odyssey's εἰς εὐνὴν τράπεθ’ ἡμέας "turn us to our bed" is a different phrase for the same request |
| λέξο (24.650, middle imperative) | "lie down" | "lie down" | "lay yourself down", "rest" |
| ἱεροὺς πυλαωρούς (24.681) | "sacred gatekeepers" | "sacred gatekeepers" | "holy", "divine" (reserved for θεῖος); follows πυλαωρός "gatekeepers" (21.530) and ἱερός "sacred" (1.366) |
| ἀνέρες ἱπποκορυσταί (24.677) | "horse-arming men" | "the men armed with horses" | follows ἱπποκορυσταί (2.1) and the published iliad-007 rendering of this very line |
| Πέργαμον (24.700) | "Pergamus" | "Pergamus" (+ note: the citadel of Troy) | "Pergamum", "Pergamon", "the citadel" |
| τοίχου τοῦ ἑτέρου (24.598) | "the other wall" | "the other wall" | "the opposite wall", "the far wall" (each decides which wall) |
| λέχος / λεχέεσσι (of Hector’s bier, 24.600, 24.702) | "a bed" (poetic plural) | "a bed" | "bier" (the Greek has "bed"), "couch" (reserved for εὐνή and κλιντήρ); follows the table's λέχος "bed" |
| ἰσάσκετο (24.607) | "made herself equal" | "had made herself the equal of" | "compared herself", "rivalled", "vied with" |
| ἐέλμεθα (κατὰ ἄστυ ἐέλμεθα, 24.662) | "we are shut in" | "we are shut up" | "besieged", "penned" (each adds a siege image the verb lacks) |
| ἐρρώσαντο (24.616, of nymphs by the Achelous) | "danced" | "dance" (+ note: ῥώομαι "move swiftly"; "dance" is the traditional sense) | "rushed", "sped" |
| ἐκνοστήσαντι (24.705) | "come home from battle" | "came home from battle" | "returned", "escaped"; follows ἐκνοστήσαντε (5.157) "home from" |
